newsitem.title: FRANCE: Air France to cut '96/97 loss, in profit in 1998.
newsitem.headline: Air France to cut '96/97 loss, in profit in 1998.

text.p: French airline company Air France is on course to narrow losses for the 1996/97 year to 200 million francs ($36.1 million), and the whole group should make a profit in the following year, chairman Christian Blanc said.
The group includes the Air France international airline and Air France Europe, the domestic and regional company.

"The company... is on the road to break-even. The objective of reducing losses to 200 million francs at the end of the current year (ending March 31) should be met," Blanc told the National Assembly committee for production and trade, minutes released on Wednesday showed.

That improvement would be made despite an unfavourable trend in fuel prices, Blanc said. The airline's financial forecasts had been based on fuel costs of $18 per barrel when the actual price had risen to $24 per barrel from $17.
The rise in the dollar had also generated extra expenses of around 200 million francs, he said.
Air France Europe, which is being merged with the main Air France airline, should see its 1996/97 loss cut to 800 million francs from 1.5 billion, he said.
"The following year should see a positive net result for the group," he said.
The main Air France airline posted a 1995/96 net loss of 2.9 billion francs despite an operating profit of 413 million. The net loss was due to restructuring charges.
The airline posted losses of eight billion francs in 1993 and four billion in 1992, Blanc said.
Air France's debt now stands at 12 billion francs compared with 36 billion at the end of 1993, thanks to the state's 20 billion franc cash injection, he said.

Production costs were still three or four percent higher than Germany's Lufthansa and 10-15 percent more than those at British Airways Plc (BA). The difference in wage costs at Air France were five or six percent higher than BA's, he said.
Productivity targets envisaged in a three-year restructuring plan ended last December have been slightly exceeded, and the company has cut unit costs by 20 percent.

The company has increased traffic between 15 percent and 18 percent since the launch last April of its hub at Paris Charles-de-Gaulle airport. Traffic should rise by 20 percent from next April when its alliances with Delta and Continental of the United States take effect, he said.
Air France expects to recruit 450 pilots as part of its development plans. Some 5,000 posts have been cut out of a total 40,000 without forced redundancies, he said.

Blanc said Air France would not register aircraft under foreign flags, "flags of convenience", but would move towards using small airlines under franchise whose costs are 30-40 percent lower than those of Air France.
-- Pierre Tran, Paris newsroom +33 1 4221 5452 ($ = 5.54 French Francs)
